lessons.title: Direction, scale and map symbols

Use a scale to turn a map distance into a ground distance

blocks.md: A **map** is a drawing of an area seen from above, on a smaller size. Maps show direction using the **compass**: the four main points are North, East, South and West, and between them are North-East, South-East, South-West and North-West. On most maps North is at the top. A **key** (or legend) explains the signs used for roads, rivers, schools and so on.

blocks.caption: The compass rose
blocks.alt: A compass rose with arrows to the north, south, east and west and the four in-between points.

blocks.title: Scale
blocks.md: The **scale** tells how much smaller the map is than the real ground. It can be a statement (1 cm to 1 km), a line scale, or a **representative fraction** such as **1 : 50 000**, which means 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm = **0.5 km** on the ground. A larger number after the colon means a smaller scale and less detail.

blocks.title: Measuring a ground distance
blocks.md:
1. Measure the distance on the map with a ruler, in cm.
2. Find what 1 cm stands for on the ground (use the scale).
3. Multiply the two numbers.
4. Give the answer in the right unit (m or km).
Example: 1 : 50 000 means 1 cm = 0.5 km, so 6 cm on the map = 6 × 0.5 = 3 km.

**Grid references.** Maps are covered by a grid of numbered vertical lines (eastings) and horizontal lines (northings). To give a **four-figure grid reference** of a square, read the number of the vertical line on its left first, then the number of the horizontal line at its bottom: first **along** the corridor, then **up** the stairs. For example, 3 then 5 gives the reference 3 5 (written 0305 or 3 5 depending on the map).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Never give the northing before the easting.
- Do not forget to convert cm on the map into km on the ground.
- Use the key: the same colour or symbol can mean different things on different maps.

blocks.title: Example 1: a road distance
blocks.statement: On a map of scale 1 : 50 000 the road from a school to a market measures 8 cm. How long is the real road?
steps: 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm on the ground = 0.5 km.

blocks.title: Example 2: a direction
blocks.statement: A hospital is north-east of a church. In which direction is the church from the hospital?
steps: Directions are opposite when we reverse the viewpoint.
The opposite of north-east is south-west.
So the church lies south-west of the hospital.

exercises.prompt: Explain why a map of scale 1 : 10 000 shows more detail than a map of scale 1 : 1 000 000 for the same area.
exercises.model: At 1 : 10 000 one centimetre stands for a short ground distance (100 m), so the area is shown larger and small features such as houses and paths fit on the map; at 1 : 1 000 000 one centimetre stands for 10 km and only big features can be drawn.
exercises.rubric: 1 mark: compare what 1 cm stands for; 1 mark: larger-scale map shows the area bigger; 1 mark: more detail possible.
